original_record.question: The solid shown on the right is made from two cubes. The small cube with edges $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ long sits on top of a bigger cube with edges $3 \mathrm{~cm}$ long. What is the surface area of the whole solid? <image1>
original_record.solution: The surface areas of the separate cubes are $6 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and $54 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$. When the smaller one sits on top of the larger, an area of $1 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ is lost from each of the two cubes; thus the surface area of the whole solid is $6+54-2=58 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$.
